input.summary: Replace Licensor's unilateral 7-year renewal option with mutual 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out and capped uplift
input.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a seven-year extension exercisable at the Licensor's sole option; our playbook allows renewal only by mutual written agreement, or 12-month renewals we can decline on 30 days' notice with uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. This aligns the renewal sentence with Articles IV.II and IV.III, which already require mutual written agreement; we can discuss a 60-day notice window and a 5% cap if helpful.

ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed for successive additional periods of twelve (12) months by mutual written agreement of the parties, provided that either party may elect not to renew by written notice given at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current period, and any increase in fees for a renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding period and three percent (3%).
